To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Arena Chapel frescoes of Giotto di Bondone, dating from the beginning of the fourteenth century, illustrate two types of embodied perception, the one biological, the other cultural, and that these two types of embodied cognition are linked respectively to the vertical and horizontal dimensions of space.
Giotto’s frescoes in the Arena Chapel provide salient illustrations for the embodied perception theory, and that the theory can be used to explain the development of Renaissance art and Modernism.

Giotto's frescoes in the Arena Chapel, Padua, provide salient examples of two types of embodiments, one universal (the result of biology and physical laws), the other culturally determined (acquired from the direction of script), and that Giotto may have prompted late Mediaeval chapel visitors to empathize with biblical characters, so they could share their humanity, resulting in a personal agency that led to the Renaissance and Modernity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how Giotto's frescoes, as a form of visual communication, were designed and perceived by the chapel-visitors.
the relationship between the human mind, the physical environment and the visual art of the Middle Ages, and how these three elements are interrelated.
how Giotto's paintings, in the context of the Arena Chapel, may have influenced the way in which the viewer's mind and body perceived the space and figures depicted in the frescoes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Giotto was the first artist to apply embodied perception in a manner that would have a profound effect on the history of western art.
the lateral dimension of Giotto's frescoes is the result of his intuitive use of embodied perception.

Giotto's frescoes, as a consequence of the artist's use of embodied perception, have the power to evoke an emotional response in the viewer, and to make him or her aware of the moral implications of human actions, and of the importance of the vertical dimension of time in our lives.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Giotto's frescoes, as a whole, are an expression of embodied perception, which, in turn, is an expression of the embodied mind.
the Arena Chapel frescoes of Giotto are a visual record of a major transition in human consciousness.

we have demonstrated that Giotto's paintings are not merely a record of a particular time and place, but also an expression of universal embodied perceptions, and as such, are still capable of affecting us today, and may even have played a role in the evolution of our species.
The main takeaway from our work is that
embodied perception can be a powerful tool for understanding the past, and that the visual arts, especially those of the Renaissance, are a rich source of embodied perceptions.
the embodied mind, with its biological and cultural determinations, is a key factor in the development of the human spirit, a concept that is central to the Christian tradition.
the visual arts have a unique role in the history of ideas, in that they can convey embodied knowledge, and thus, can be a source of scientific insight.
